title: One-way bound implies interactive bound
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a two-argument function whose output type $\alpha$ is finite and nonempty, and let $n \in \bbn$. If the one-way deterministic communication complexity of $f$ is at most $n$, then the (interactive) deterministic communication complexity of $f$ is at most $n + \lceil \log_2 \abs{\alpha} \rceil$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a function X → Y → α
one-way communication complexity of f is at most n
replaced:
If the one-way communication complexity of $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ is at most $n$, then
the (interactive) deterministic communication complexity of $f$ is at most
$n + \lceil \log_2 |\alpha| \rceil$, with the additive term accounting for Bob's cost
of transmitting the decoded output in the interactive model.
